items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: And Helen Dance had talked about her role in that.

ctx.x: No. He wasn’t. Not at all. No. He just wasn’t. They talk about that accident that happened, the car accident, which after that he seemed very aloof and not really interested much in promoting the band very much. But even before that I kind of wonder how much of a leader he really was. I mean he didn’t have an Irving Mills like Ellington had or Cab Calloway, somebody like that. I mean Hammond sort of came in at some point and sort of tried to take the band, do stuff with the band and stuff, and get them recording…

Well a question — I don’t know if I would have had it back then — but I’ve never really been clear about Benny Goodman’s role with this integration thing and how that happened. And you had said something to me yesterday about it. And Helen Dance had talked about her role in that. But what’s your take on exactly how it happened.

Well my take on it is sort of what I’ve gotten from reading various books and articles. So I mean I wasn’t there so I can’t say I have any firsthand knowledge, but I just got the impression that, you know, he wanted these two musicians in his organization. He wanted Wilson and he wanted Hampton. But he was smart enough to know that if he put them in the full big band it was going to cause problems. Not that they weren’t going to cause problems anyway having them as a sideshow, but I think it caused less problems…
